text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Luxembourg's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Poos in Beirut on a one-day visit. Lebanon's participation in peace talks with Israel is very important, he said upon his arrival.
-Hariri told paliamentary deputies that his government did not plan to hand over to the private sector posts and telecommunication services.
-The weather to improve as of Friday evening after heavy rain and snow covered most of Lebanon.
-The possibility of lifting the 12-year-old U.S. travel ban on Lebanon is under discussion in Washington.
-The Lebanese Banks Association slashed the Lebanese pound prime lending rate to 18 percent from 24 percent. It will discuss with the Bank of Lebanon the issue of adjusting treasury bill yields.
-Pilots at Lebanon's national carrier Middle East Airlines plan to go on a one-day strike next Tuesday.
-The Council for Development and Reconstruction said in a report that foreign financing of reconstruction and development projects in Lebanon since 1993 reached $3,125 million.
-Hizbollah said that Palestinian President Arafat made humiliating concessions to Israelis in a deal for partial Israeli withdrawal from the West Bank town of Hebron.
